Flowchart branch header 'Sudden collapse'. The branch is defined by timing relative to the vaccination (at the time of vaccination vs 5-10 minutes after). The grammar only compares an onset/timestamp_of_event with time_ago (now-relative); it cannot compare the collapse's onset with the vaccination's time, so the branch itself cannot be expressed. The builders instead split the branches on the clinical features (BP, pulse, wheeze/stridor/cough, swelling/rash), which is the only available approximation. Noted under rule-level problems.

elements.scope_reason: The feature list that leads to 'Fainting episode likely'. Six parts, judged separately below.
parts_missing: Part 1 'Occurs suddenly, at the time of vaccination (before, during or immediately after)': not_representable (timing relative to vaccination); not encoded, correctly so.

Part 2 'Loss of consciousness usually lasts 20 seconds to 1 minute and is relieved by lying patient down and raising legs': missing. The duration has no unit in the language, and 'relieved by' is a response to intervention, so a literal encoding is impossible; but SNOMED has (snomed_concept "Brief loss of consciousness" "finding") and (snomed_concept "Prolonged loss of consciousness" "finding"), which would have carried the page's '< 1 minute' vs '> 1 minute' split as a check_for finding. Neither is used.

Part 3 'BP is: briefly low but rapidly normal again': partial. Encoded as SBP >= 90 and DBP >= 60 (the complement of the delayed branch's < 90/60). The page allows a transient low BP in fainting; the rule excludes fainting whenever the recorded BP is low, and the sister rule then calls it anaphylaxis. 'Rapidly normal again' needs a repeat measurement and is not representable, so this is an accepted approximation, but it is lossy in the direction of over-calling anaphylaxis.

Part 6 'No other signs or symptoms present': partial. Only the five delayed-branch signs (wheeze, stridor, cough, swelling, rash) are excluded with (no ...). 'No other signs or symptoms' is broader; at minimum Difficulty breathing / Dyspnea (a recorded common symptom and the anaphylaxis page's breathing sign) is not excluded.

The whole rule reduces the page's six features to 'collapse + vaccination + none of the delayed-branch signs + normal BP + pulse <= 120'.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable anaphylaxis after collapse following vaccination
rule_level_problems.problem: Any single item of the `or` is sufficient, and Cough is one of them. Cough is a routine common symptom, so a patient with a cold who faints at vaccination gets probable Anaphylaxis, and (symmetrically) is excluded from the fainting rule by its (no Cough). The page lists cough only as something the breathing 'may' show, alongside wheeze and stridor; it does not make cough alone a discriminator. Cough should at least be paired with another sign (or dropped from both rules).

The page's primary discriminator, timing (sudden/at the time of vaccination vs 5-10 minutes after, up to 1 hour) and the duration of loss of consciousness (< 1 minute vs > 1 minute), is absent from both rules. Timing relative to the vaccination is genuinely not representable, but the duration split could have been approximated with the existing SNOMED findings 'Brief loss of consciousness' and 'Prolonged loss of consciousness' as check_for items used as evidence. Without them the two rules split purely on BP, pulse and five signs.

No system_priority_evaluation. The red box 'Treat as anaphylaxis' is the page's escalation and the house standard turns the red box into an Urgent priority (referencing (active_condition Anaphylaxis)). The file depends on the anaphylaxis page providing that rule; if it does, this is fine, but it is not visible from this page and the file does not say so.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable fainting episode following vaccination
rule_level_problems.problem: The rule requires SBP >= 90, DBP >= 60 and pulse <= 120 as positive evidence. If BP or pulse has not been recorded (collapse is often seen before vitals are taken), the comparisons cannot be satisfied and the fainting rule never fires, while the anaphylaxis rule may fire on a single sign. Also the page allows a 'briefly low' BP in fainting; a BP recorded during that window makes the rules call anaphylaxis instead. Both are consequences of the measurement-only approximation; worth a note for the clinician reviewer.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable fainting episode following vaccination
rule_level_problems.problem: 'No other signs or symptoms present' is encoded only as the absence of the five delayed-branch signs. Difficulty breathing / Dyspnea (a recorded common symptom and the anaphylaxis page's breathing criterion) is excluded from neither rule, so a collapsed patient with difficulty breathing but no wheeze/stridor/cough and normal vitals is called fainting.

The 'Refer if' criteria (head injury, known heart condition or serious illness, chest pain, shortness of breath, confusion, blurred vision, difficulty talking) are not collected or used. Scope is arguable (referral is management), but these are findings the page tells the health worker to look for after a faint and the check_for does not ask for them.

summary: The red box is captured as a probable Anaphylaxis rule with the right concepts and thresholds (BP < 90/60, pulse > 120, wheeze, stridor, cough, swelling, rash), and 'Fainting episode likely' as its mutually exclusive probable Syncope complement; every SNOMED concept resolves and every check_for item is used. The most consequential problems are that Cough alone triggers probable anaphylaxis (and alone excludes fainting) although the page never makes cough a discriminator, and that the page's main axis, timing and duration of loss of consciousness, is absent: timing relative to vaccination is not representable, but the > 1 minute split could have used the existing 'Brief/Prolonged loss of consciousness' findings. There is no priority evaluation on the page, so the red box's urgency depends on the anaphylaxis page's rule; the referral criteria and the CPR escalation are not encoded.
